name: Anbang Insurance

summary.text: Anbang Insurance Group was a Chinese insurer founded and chaired by Wu Xiaohui that became known for overseas trophy acquisitions, including the Waldorf Astoria hotel in New York, bought from Hilton Worldwide in October 2014 for $1.95 billion. In early 2017 it negotiated with Kushner Companies over an investment in 666 Fifth Avenue; the talks ended on March 29, 2017. On February 23, 2018 the China Insurance Regulatory Commission seized control of Anbang, citing a risk of insolvency, and Wu was prosecuted; in May 2018 a Shanghai court sentenced him to 18 years for fundraising fraud and embezzlement. The state injected 60.8 billion yuan of capital, and in 2019 a new entity, Dajia Insurance Group, was formed to take over Anbang's healthy assets; the regulatory takeover ended in February 2020. The Kushner Companies file on this site records the 666 Fifth talks; this file holds the company's own record.

facts.claim: On February 23, 2018 the China Insurance Regulatory Commission announced it was taking control of Anbang for one year, saying it was acting to protect insurance consumers because Anbang was in danger of insolvency; chairman Wu Xiaohui was removed from his post and prosecuted for economic crimes.
facts.quote: Wu Xiaohui has been removed from his post and is being prosecuted for "economic crimes."

sources.title: China seizes control of Anbang Insurance as chairman prosecuted
China seizes control of Anbang Insurance as chairman prosecuted

facts.claim: In May 2018 a Shanghai court sentenced Wu Xiaohui to 18 years in prison for fundraising fraud and embezzlement, deprived him of political rights for four years and ordered 10.5 billion yuan of his assets confiscated; prosecutors cited illegal fundraising of 65.2 billion yuan and embezzlement of 10 billion yuan of Anbang funds, and the court found he had submitted counterfeit financial statements to the regulator. Wu appealed.
facts.quote: Wu will be deprived of his political rights for four years, and 10.5 billion yuan ($1.7 billion) of his assets will be confiscated

facts.claim: In April 2018 the Chinese government injected 60.8 billion yuan of capital into Anbang to bolster its solvency, and in June-July 2019 a new company, Dajia Insurance Group, with 20.4 billion yuan of registered capital and 98.2 percent owned by the China Insurance Security Fund, was established to take over Anbang's life, pension and asset-management businesses; the regulator ended its two-year takeover in February 2020.
facts.quote: Beijing-based Dajia Insurance Group, which was established on June 25, has 20.4 billion yuan ($3 billion) in registered capital
